questions.q: What is the four-step performance tuning loop this lesson describes?
options: Measure, identify, change, verify
Guess, apply, hope, move on
Index everything, then check results
Change first, then measure to see if it helped
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names this loop and ties it to the same discipline used on every earlier platform in this path.

questions.q: Which PostgreSQL tool aggregates execution statistics across every query the server has run, helping you find the worst offenders during the measure step?
options: pg_stat_statements
pg_basebackup
pg_dumpall
psql alone, with no extension needed
questions.explain: pg_stat_statements aggregates stats across all queries, unlike EXPLAIN ANALYZE which examines one query at a time.

questions.q: What does EXPLAIN ANALYZE's plan output help you do during the identify step, per this lesson?
options: Show exactly which operator is expensive, such as a sequential scan or a sort spilling to disk
Automatically fix the query without further input
List every user connected to the database
Archive WAL segments
questions.explain: The plan output traces the slow query down to a specific expensive operator, which is what the identify step needs.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why is 'just add an index' or 'just increase memory' considered guessing rather than tuning?
options: Because it skips measuring and identifying the actual cause before making a change
Because indexes never help PostgreSQL performance
Because increasing memory is always harmful
Because PostgreSQL doesn't support configuration changes
questions.explain: Without measuring first and identifying a specific cause, a change might not address the real bottleneck at all.

questions.q: What does the verify step in this methodology actually confirm?
options: That the change actually helped and didn't make something else worse
That the backup completed successfully
That a new index was created without checking its effect
That the server restarted cleanly
questions.explain: Verify means re-measuring after the change to confirm real improvement, not just assuming the change worked.
